paragraphs.text: Cheadeb presents The Canteville Ghost by Oscar Wilde.
Part 1. The Stain
Mr. Hiram B. Otis was American.
He was very rich and very important.
He wanted to live in an old house in England,
so he decided to buy Canteville Chase, the home of Lord Canteville.
Everyone told him that he was doing a very foolish thing.
Canteville Chase is haunted, they said.
Lord Canteville himself warned Mr. Otis about the ghost.
Many members of my family have seen the ghost.
My grand aunt, the Duchess, was dressing for dinner one night.
Suddenly, the hands of a skeleton touched her on the shoulders.
She has never recovered from the shock.
My wife, Lady Canteville, cannot sleep at night because of the mysterious noises in the house.
My Lord said Mr. Otis.
I will pay you extra for the ghost.
I come from a modern democratic country.
If we find a ghost, we'll put it in a museum or a show for everyone to see.
Lord Canteville smiled.
The ghost really exists.
People have seen it many times in the last 300 years.
Since 50-84, in fact, it always appears before the death of any member of my family.
In my home, joked Mr. Otis.
The doctor appears before the death of any member of my family.
I am an American.
He continued.
Americans don't believe in ghosts.
They are an old-fashioned European idea.
If you don't mind having a ghost in the house, that's all right.
But please remember that I have warned you.
A few weeks later, Lord Canteville sold Canteville Chase to the Americans.
There were six people in the Otis family.
Mr. Otis himself was a United States government minister.
He was a strong Democrat.
His wife, Mrs. Lucretia Otis, was a good-looking, middle-aged lady.
When she had been a young woman in New York, she had been famous for her beauty.
She was full of energy and very healthy.
Their eldest son was called Washington.
He was tall, fair-haired and handsome.
He liked dancing very much.
His sister, Virginia, was 15 years old.
She was lovely.
Her large blue eyes had a spirit of freedom.
She loved riding her pony in the country.
A young English lord, Cecil, the Duke of Cheshire, was in love with her.
The youngest children were twins, Ricky and Robbie.
They were often naughty, but everybody liked them.
When the family came to live at the house, they drove through the woods in a carriage.
It was a lovely July evening.
The birds were singing.
Squirrels looked at them from the trees.
Rapids ran away over the grass.
However, as they approached cantaville chase, the weather changed.
Dark clouds appeared.
Some large black birds flew over their heads.
It began to rain.
In the garden, they saw a black tree with no leaves or flowers on it.
An old woman, dressed in black, with a white apron and cap, was waiting for them at the door of the house.
This was Mrs. Amni, the housekeeper.
Welcome to cantaville chase.
She said they followed her through the dark wooden hall into the library.
Tea was ready for them.
What's that?
Asked Mrs. Otis suddenly.
There was a dark red stain on the floor by the fireplace.
It is...lot.
Replied the old housekeeper.
How horrible.
Said Mrs. Otis.
I don't like blood stains in the sitting room.
Remove it.
Mrs. Amni smiled.
It is the blood of Lady Elianor de Cantaville.
Her husband, Sir Simon de Cantaville, murdered her on that exact spot in 1575.
Sir Simon disappeared nine years later.
Nobody has ever found his body.
But his guilty spirit still holds cantaville chase.
And nobody can remove the stain.
Nonsense.
Fried Washington.
Pinkerton's champion cleaner will clean it away.
It's the latest American technology.
He knelt down and rubbed the floor with the champion cleaner.
In a few moments, the blood had disappeared.
I knew Pinkerton's would do it.
He said triumphantly.
At that moment, there was a great flash of lightning.
There was a boom of thunder.
Everyone was frightened.
The ghost is angry.
Fried Mrs. Amni.
And she fainted.
The English climate is really terrible.
Said Mr. Otis calmly lighting a cigar.
I'm not surprised that everyone wants to leave the country to go to live in America.
Look at Mrs. Amni.
Said his wife.
She's fainted.
What a useless housekeeper.
Will reduce her wages.
Said Mr. Otis.
As soon as he said that, Mrs. Amni recovered.
Don't laugh at the ghosts, sir.
I have seen terrible things in this house.
We are Americans.
Said Mr. Otis.
We're not afraid of ghosts.
You're safe with us.
Added Mrs. Otis.
Now let's all go to bed.
